data: This course will introduce psychoanalysis, focusing on the groundbreaking work of Sigmund Freud that transformed our understanding of mental life in the late 19th century. Although psychoanalysis is often associated with sex, it actually encompasses a broader exploration of societal pressures and the ideologies surrounding sex and sexuality. Freud challenged prevailing psychiatric and psychological models by introducing the concept of the unconscious. Psychoanalysis provides a unique framework to delve into the internal divisions of human subjectivity, particularly through the study of the unconscious in clinical settings. Moreover, it offers valuable insights into the influence of culture and social forces on the construction of individual difference. The course will examine the dynamic interplay between individuals and society, the intersection of clinical practice and cultural context, and the complexities of sexuality and sexual differences. Students will have the opportunity to analyze and critique Freud's theories and methods, encouraging a critical examination of his work while also exploring how contemporary psychoanalysts continue to build upon and refine his ideas.
